# No recursion, no goto, bounded loops

The space profile (`space-profile-invariants` rule) requires recursion-free, goto-free code with bounded loops. To avoid two parallel coding styles, the same rule applies to **all** slave code (both profiles). Stricter than MISRA C:2023's mandatory + required set; advisory-grade enforced.

## Banned constructs

```c
goto label;                            // banned everywhere in slave/

void f(int n) { if (n) f(n - 1); }     // direct recursion banned

void a(); void b() { a(); }            // mutual recursion banned
void a() { b(); }
```

## Required: bounded loops

Every loop must have a compile-time-known upper bound or an explicit runtime bound asserted before entry. The bound must be small enough to fit the slave's tick budget (see [`docs/adr/drafts/adr-0010-packet-loss-tolerance-budget.md`](../../docs/adr/drafts/adr-0010-packet-loss-tolerance-budget.md) for tick-rate budgets).

```c
/* Good */
for (size_t i = 0; i < TETHYS_ODT_MAX_ENTRIES; ++i) { ... }   // compile-time bound

assert(n <= TETHYS_MAX_BURST_LOSS);                            // runtime-bounded
for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) { ... }

/* Banned */
while (true) { ... }              // unless explicit `break` within bounded iteration
while (ptr != NULL) { ... }       // bound not visible; refactor or document
```

## Rationale

- ECSS-E-ST-40C Rev.1 (S18) requires worst-case-execution-time bounds for safety-critical loops.
- ISO 26262:2018 Part 6 (S9 in standards matrix) requires structured control flow for ASIL B+.
- MISRA C:2023 Rule 15.1 (advisory) bans `goto` outright.

## CI enforcement (lands in PR-4)

`misra-gate.yml` runs cppcheck with `-DMISRA_RULES=15.1,15.4,15.5,15.6` and treats violations as errors.
